list.landscapeHint: The landscape is a world of regions: regions form by themselves from what depends on what (“Must be known first”) — topics that share a lot lie together. Each level shows a handful to a dozen or so fields; tapping a region opens its map. Height is the number of steps still to climb: a valley — you know it, one step — you can start now. Rename a region on the map (“Rename”), and move a topic to another region in its pop-up.
list.quiltHint: Progress map: each entry is a tile in the colour of how well you know it — grouped as in “Selection and groups” (e.g. ideas by lesson, lessons under chapters). Learners see it in Progress and in the “View” module on a page.
list.searchStartTitle: View opened from one entry — search works in the whole display
list.setInSchemes: Set up this display in Schemes…
list.learnThis: Learn this — a review in Learning
list.adjust: Adjust — what and how to show
list.fromEntryNote: (search, kind and filter — in the whole display)
list.matrixHint: Choose the rows and columns of the matrix in “Selection and groups”.
list.planOf: To the plan of which text
list.canvasHint: Save the view so the places on the canvas stay — all authors see them.
list.selectHint: Selecting: checkbox, Ctrl+click, Shift+click or dragging over the checkboxes; on a phone, press and hold an entry.
list.outlineHint: The structure also shows what lies beneath the entries — in “Selection” add the step “Follow the structure” (along fields the kind marks as a structure link) or “Follow a reference”.
list.readerChooses: as the reader chooses (Thomas’s article: text)
list.samePlaceBy: At the same place in the work — by

who.title: Who sees it
who.renamed: {count} of them got a new key (the old one was taken there) — links go by identifier, so nothing broke.
who.moveHint: This is how publishing works now: to make something public, move it to a base in an open area (to make it private — to a base in a closed area). The identifier stays, so links keep working. Learners’ answers stay with this base.
who.optOpenArea: {name} — open area, base not opened yet
who.afterMove: After the move it is read by: {audience}.
who.opensWarn: The base “{name}” is public as a whole: everyone will see this entry and {whole} of that base.
who.needsMore: Needs from this base ({count}): {list} and {more} others.
who.moveAlongPublic: Move them along with it (they will become public too)
who.stayHere: They stay here — whoever reads only “{name}” will see “[reference unavailable]” in their place.
who.tooMany: This base already has {max} sources — “{name}” will not be added; what you move will disappear from view here.
who.asSource: “{base}” will get “{name}” as a source — it still sees everything you move there.
who.understoodPublic: I understand: this will be public.
who.inside: {entries} entries (including {questions} questions with answers), {revisions} reviews, {flows} paths
who.members: It is read by members of the area “{area}” (and those they gave a link or a seat).
who.ifOpen: If this area became open, everyone would read {whole}. To share only a part, create a separate base in an open area and move the chosen entries there (entry → Who sees it → Move).
who.openArea: The area “{area}” is open: everyone reads {whole} — currently {inside}.
who.keepForSome: Anything that should stay for chosen people, move to a base in a closed area (entry → Who sees it → Move).
who.notOpened: The area “{area}” is open, but this base is not opened yet — until you open it, only area members read it.
who.afterOpen: Once opened, anyone — without an account — will read {whole}: currently {inside}. Modules on pages will show it to everyone.
who.partOnly: If only a part should be public, don’t open this base: create a separate one in this area and move the chosen entries there.
who.copiesFirst: First withdraw the old publication copies (below): this base still has copies stored in entries.
who.understoodWhole: I understand: the whole base will be public.
who.openForAll: Open the whole base to everyone
who.oldCopiesHint: From the time when the base published single entries, copies remain — on the server and stored in entries. Nothing uses them any more. Withdrawing leaves the entries themselves; a copy showing an entry that no longer exists stays.

parts.question: Question
parts.addMethodsHint: A way of adding creates several linked entries at once — e.g. a passage of Scripture and a commentary on it, or a word with its translation — row by row.
parts.noKinds: This base has no entry kinds of its own yet.
parts.methodsHint: Each way can create entries of several kinds at once and link them with references; several ways can create the same kind. A kind needs no way of its own — you can always add a single entry.
parts.noMethods: No ways of adding yet. “+ Form” starts from the kind you want to add.
parts.viewsHint: A display says what to show (kinds, filter, then along references — e.g. a commentary with arguments for and against) and how (table, tree, matrix, canvas). It can combine entries of many kinds; not every kind needs one of its own.
parts.noViews: No displays yet. Entries always shows all entries as a table.
parts.learnFrom: Learning from this entry: its cards as a review.

tabs.schemaKindsSays: Which entries exist: their fields and references to other entries.
tabs.schemaAddSays: How knowledge is entered — also several linked entries of different kinds at once.
tabs.schemaViewsSays: What to show and how — also information from entries that references lead to.

home.makeDaily: Create a “Daily review” from all cards
home.openingBase: Opening the base and its sources…
